chapter: Quality Serenaders, Cotton Club and union recollections
title: Frank Sebastian, the Green Mill and the New Cotton Club
summary: Howard describes Sebastian as a flashy sport who kept wanting his band, and agrees the New Cotton Club was at Culver City.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: It says here that Frank Sebastian must have done a very good business with the Quality Band, for in 1927 he bought the Green Mill Club, a huge barn-like building and redecorated the new club in the swank manner of those days, and the Quality Serenaders opened the New Cotton Club. So there was the little Cotton Club that was the former Nightingale, and
then the New Cotton Club had formerly been the Green Mill, is that right?
I don't remember that now.
But your band --
I forget that one, because all I can remember is the Green Mill.
Uh-huh. Was that the Culver City location?
Yes, Culver City.
What kind of a person was Frank Sebastian?
What kind of person was he?
Uh-huh.

He was a -- I don't know what you call it, but he was a very smart aleck man, and he wore clothes, boy, I'm telling you, he just dressed up like nobody's business. And he come out there and he'd get out on the stand and put his hands on his hips and (Inaudible). A lot of the people were on there.
Stand. Suzie worked for him.
Was he a pretty fair person to work for?
Oh, yeah, he was pretty nice. A pretty nice person. He was real nice. But he was a sport, that's all.
Uh-huh.
That's all I can tell you about him. A sport, and he come around and worried the dickens out of me.

"Bring the band over, bring the band over, bring the band over, that's all he did. Always wanted to get a band. I used to be running back and forth from the Cotton Club to the Nightingale, yeah, it was the Nightingale. Yeah, that's what it was. He had a band in there.
Would you hold the mike up please?
Uh-huh. It was your band, right?
Yeah. The Nightingale.
Did he run some club here before he bought the Nightingale, or was that the first time you knew him, when he came in and bought the Nightingale?
Who?
Frank Sebastian.
No, I knew him before then.
What was he doing before he bought the Nightingale?
Before he bought it?
Uh-huh. Was he running another club?
No, just the same thing. Fooling around with bands, you know. Wasn't doing anything different.
But he didn't have another club before the Nightingale. Was the Nightingale his first club?
Yeah, the Nightingale was his first club. That was the first one.
I see. Because I've heard his name a lot in association with the Cotton Club in Culver City, but I
didn't know about the Little Cotton Club before that.
The Little Cotton Club?
Yeah.
Well, that's what they called it.
That's interesting.
Ain't that something?
Yeah.
You can correct that.
